# Requirements Quality Checklist: Approvals that carry a decision, guided pipeline repair, and a uniform question standard

**Purpose**: Validate that this feature's requirements are complete, clear, consistent and objectively verifiable before planning commits to an approach
**Created**: 2026-09-05
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Review result — 2026-09-05

**12 of 45 satisfied. 33 open.** Every item carries its verdict inline: `[x]` with the evidence that satisfies it, unchecked with `**Open**:` naming what is missing.

| Section                         | Satisfied | Open |
| ------------------------------- | --------- | ---- |
| Requirement Clarity             | 4 / 10    | 6    |
| Requirement Measurability       | 3 / 9     | 6    |
| Requirement Consistency         | 3 / 7     | 4    |
| Requirement Completeness — gaps | 1 / 11    | 10   |
| Dependencies & Assumptions      | 0 / 4     | 4    |
| Scenario Coverage               | 1 / 4     | 3    |

**Who reviewed this, and the caveat that matters.** Evaluated by Claude Code at the maintainer's explicit request, which is the one condition `speckit-checklist` permits agent evaluation under. The same agent drafted most of the specification, so this is not an independent review: every `[x]` is a claim that specific text exists at a specific place, never a claim that the requirement is good. Each is written to be spot-checkable in one lookup, and a reviewer disagreeing with any of them should re-open it.

### What the open items are, in shape

- **Five of the open items were already answered and simply never ticked** is _not_ the finding. The reverse is true: only CHK004, CHK005, CHK011 and CHK013 were settled by this feature's own R1–R3 research, and they are now ticked. Most of the rest are real.
- **Ten of the 33 are unaddressed edge cases in the pipeline capability and in recovery flows** — CHK030–CHK032, CHK037, CHK041–CHK044 cluster there. That is the newest and least-exercised part of the feature, and this repository runs no pipeline to exercise it against (CHK040).
- **Several are one-clause fixes rather than research.** CHK012 needs SC-010 to reference R2's floor; CHK009 needs FR-010 to name the two forges; CHK018 needs FR-031 to point at where the limits live; CHK029 needs FR-013 to state a minimum. In each case the substance exists elsewhere and the requirement does not point at it.
- **CHK026 found a real mismatch, not just an imprecision.** FR-032 covers feature 006's requirements "that mandate an approval before every phase", which fits 006 FR-010 and FR-011. The Supersession record also supersedes **006 FR-013**, which governs what a proposal states rather than whether it is approved. No requirement in this feature accounts for that supersession.

### What was deliberately not done

Closing the open items. The maintainer scoped this run to evaluation, and amending a merged specification on gaps the same agent both found and would fix is a larger decision than a checklist pass. The open items are written as a work list for whoever takes that on.

## Requirement Clarity — terms that carry the decision

- [ ] CHK001 Is "readily undone" defined normatively rather than only in Assumptions, given FR-002 and FR-003 both turn on it? [Clarity, Spec §FR-002] **Open**: defined only under Assumptions — "undone by the maintainer without recovering data or contacting a remote service" — and Assumptions is not normative text. FR-002 enumerates the always-gate set, which covers the practical cases, and `contracts/gate-decision.md` fixes it; neither is a definition inside the requirements.
- [x] CHK002 Is "differs in any way from what the maintainer approved in the plan" specified precisely enough to decide a borderline case — reworded but equivalent, reordered, or a differing artifact list? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-001] **Reviewed 2026-09-05**: yes. FR-001 says "differs **in any way**", which decides every borderline the item lists by making all of them gate — reworded-but-equivalent, reordered, and a differing artifact list each differ, so each asks. A broad rule, but a decidable one.
- [ ] CHK003 Is "the plan" the maintainer approved identified as a specific named artifact, so that FR-001's comparison has two defined sides? [Clarity, Spec §FR-001] **Open**: "the plan" is never named as an artifact. FR-006 requires every phase's argument drafted before the first phase runs, which is the thing FR-001 compares against, but no requirement says so — FR-001's comparison has one defined side.
- [x] CHK004 Is "normative" defined, given FR-028, FR-029 and SC-010 all rest on distinguishing normative text from other text? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-028] **Reviewed 2026-09-05**: yes. `research.md` R1 gives six mechanical categories plus "every fenced code block is normative in its entirety", and `.claude/rules/repository-docs.md` § What "normative content" means restates it as governing text. `scripts/compaction-audit.sh` implements it.
- [x] CHK005 Is the boundary between a "deliberate, reviewed revision pass" and "incidental reformatting during unrelated work" stated in decidable terms, given that distinction is the entire content of FR-025? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-025] **Reviewed 2026-09-05**: yes. `.claude/rules/repository-docs.md` § The one exception gives four conditions, all decidable: the change's stated purpose, an audit verdict, no normative content dropped, no section reordered or retitled.
- [ ] CHK006 Is "verified fix" defined, or does FR-009 rely on the reader inferring it from the bug-remediation workflow's own vocabulary? [Clarity, Spec §FR-009] **Open**: "verified fix" is nowhere defined. FR-015 names the three records and FR-016 refers to "validation does not show the defect resolved", so the term is inferable from the bug workflow's vocabulary — which is exactly what the item asks about.
- [ ] CHK007 Is "a cause outside the repository's own content" bounded — does a dependency pinned in the repository but broken upstream fall inside or outside? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-018] **Open**: unbounded. The Edge Cases entry gives three examples — an outage, a credential expiry, a runner fault — and settles no boundary. A dependency pinned in the repository but broken upstream falls in neither the examples nor any stated rule.
- [ ] CHK008 Is "no default is defensible" given any criterion, or is FR-023's escape hatch available whenever a recommendation is inconvenient to produce? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-023] **Open**: FR-023 supplies no criterion. "The decision is the maintainer's alone and no default is defensible" is self-referential, so the escape hatch is available whenever a recommendation is inconvenient to produce.
- [ ] CHK009 Are "both forges the toolkit already supports" named in the specification, rather than requiring the reader to consult the codebase to know FR-010's scope? [Completeness, Spec §FR-010] **Open**: neither FR-010 nor the Assumptions entry names GitHub or GitLab. Both say "the two forges the toolkit supports", so FR-010's scope requires reading the codebase.
- [x] CHK010 Is "before it begins" in FR-011c anchored to a specific point, distinguishable from FR-011's "before proposing a cause"? [Clarity, Spec §FR-011c] **Reviewed 2026-09-05**: yes, and the two are distinguishable. FR-011c's "before it begins" anchors to the capability's own start; FR-011's anchors to before a cause is proposed, which is later. SC-012 states the same contrast as "before the run begins" versus "partway through".

## Requirement Measurability — can a reviewer check it?

- [x] CHK011 Does FR-027 state how much shortening is required, or would removing one character satisfy it? [Measurability, Spec §FR-027] **Reviewed 2026-09-05**: yes, since `research.md` R2 — at least 15% of non-code, non-frontmatter, non-blank characters, stated normatively in `.claude/rules/repository-docs.md` § The length floor. This item is one of the five that forced R1–R3. FR-027 is separately withdrawn, but the measurability question is answered either way.
- [ ] CHK012 Does SC-010's "shorter than its previous version" express the intended outcome, given it is satisfied by a trivial reduction? [Acceptance Criteria, Spec §SC-010] **Open**, and narrowly so. R2's floor answers the substance, but **SC-010's own text was never amended to reference it** — read alone, "shorter than its previous version" is still satisfied by removing one character. The fix is one clause in SC-010, not new research.
- [x] CHK013 Is there a stated procedure by which FR-029's "establishable by comparison" is carried out, or does it rest on a judgement no procedure produces? [Measurability, Spec §FR-029] **Reviewed 2026-09-05**: yes. `research.md` R3 names the procedure, `scripts/compaction-audit.sh` is it, and `contracts/compaction-audit-cli.md` specifies its invocation, output and verdicts. A reviewer runs a command rather than exercising judgement.
- [ ] CHK014 Does SC-001's "strictly fewer than the number of phases" capture the intent, given it is satisfied by removing exactly one approval out of eight? [Acceptance Criteria, Spec §SC-001] **Open**: SC-001 is satisfied by 7 approvals out of 8. `contracts/gate-decision.md` fixes the always-gate set at six boundaries, which is the real intent, but SC-001's own threshold does not express it.
- [ ] CHK015 Can SC-002 be evaluated after the fact — is a run required to record, per phase, which condition applied? [Measurability, Spec §SC-002] **Open**: SC-002 claims it is "verifiable by inspecting a completed run's record", but no requirement obliges the run to record, per phase, which condition applied. FR-004 requires announcing a reason in the run's output, which is not the same as a durable record.
- [ ] CHK016 Is FR-034's "re-examined and its outcome recorded" verifiable, or could any statement whatsoever satisfy it? [Measurability, Spec §FR-034] **Open**: "re-examined and its outcome recorded" is satisfied by any statement whatsoever. The re-examination did happen and is at `research.md` R9, but FR-034 as written would have accepted a sentence asserting it.
- [ ] CHK017 Is SC-009's "stated in exactly one place" checkable given the standard's wording may legitimately be quoted or referenced elsewhere? [Measurability, Spec §SC-009] **Open**: SC-009's "stated in exactly one place" and "zero restatements" do not distinguish a restatement from a legitimate pointer. The check as run greps for the old sentence, which finds restatements of that wording and nothing else.
- [ ] CHK018 Are the "length, structure and formatting limits the repository already places on these documents" enumerated or referenced by location, so FR-031 can be checked? [Completeness, Spec §FR-031] **Open**: FR-031 names no location. The limits exist — `.claude/rules/skill-authoring.md` § The three budgets and `.claude/rules/repository-docs.md` § Markdown mechanics — but the requirement points at neither, so checking it requires knowing where to look.
- [x] CHK019 Can SC-007's "makes no source-file change of its own" be established by observation, or only by reading the implementation? [Measurability, Spec §SC-007] **Reviewed 2026-09-05**: yes, by observation. FR-015 guarantees `fix.md` exists and records what the bug workflow changed; any source change in the tree absent from that list is the capability's own. Comparing the two is observation, not implementation reading.

## Requirement Consistency

- [x] CHK020 Do User Story 1's acceptance scenario 1 and FR-003 agree? **Resolved 2026-09-05**: they did not. The scenario conditioned auto-proceeding on the phase writing "only specification artifacts", while FR-003 conditions it on FR-001 and FR-002 not applying. FR-003 governs; the scenario was amended to test reversibility instead. [Conflict, Spec §US1, §FR-003]
- [x] CHK021 Does FR-008's skip reporting interact consistently with FR-003 — is announcing a skip a form of the FR-004 announcement, a separate obligation, or an approval point in its own right? [Consistency, Spec §FR-008, §FR-004] **Reviewed 2026-09-05**: yes. FR-008's "whether or not an approval was requested for it" makes skip reporting unconditional, which settles it as a separate obligation: FR-004 fires only when proceeding under FR-003, and a skipped phase is not a phase proceeding. Neither is it an approval point.
- [ ] CHK022 Is FR-020's "every point at which any of the toolkit's workflows requires a decision" consistent with FR-002's list of steps that always require approval, or do the two overlap without saying so? [Consistency, Spec §FR-020, §FR-002] **Open**: they overlap and neither says so. FR-020 covers every decision point in every workflow; FR-002 names steps that always require approval in one of them. FR-002's steps are a subset of FR-020's points, and no requirement states the relationship.
- [ ] CHK023 Do FR-016 (offer a return to diagnosis, uncapped) and FR-013 (offer alternatives before changing anything) state whether a second cycle re-runs the FR-012 and FR-013 approvals or reuses the first cycle's answers? [Gap, Spec §FR-016] **Open**: FR-016 says the return to diagnosis is offered and uncapped, and says nothing about whether a second cycle re-runs FR-012's root-cause approval and FR-013's choice of approach or reuses the first cycle's answers.
- [ ] CHK024 Is FR-014's "MUST NOT edit source files itself" consistent with FR-011b's fallback, in which the maintainer supplies output — does supplied output enter the record the same way retrieved output does? [Consistency, Spec §FR-014, §FR-011b] **Open**: FR-011b requires reporting which case occurred and obtaining the output, and nothing states whether maintainer-supplied evidence enters the record the way retrieved evidence does. FR-015 covers the three records but not the provenance of the evidence in them.
- [x] CHK025 Are FR-024 ("recorded once, in a single place") and FR-020–FR-023 consistent about whether individual workflows may restate any part of the standard for local emphasis? [Consistency, Spec §FR-024] **Reviewed 2026-09-05**: yes, consistent and explicit. FR-024 says "recorded once, in a single place ... **rather than restated in each workflow**", which names restatement as the thing forbidden; SC-009 measures it as "zero restatements". FR-020–FR-023 state the standard's content and claim no local home for it.
- [ ] CHK026 Do FR-032 and FR-033 together account for every requirement of feature 006 that this feature touches, leaving none silently unaddressed? [Completeness, Spec §FR-032, §FR-033] **Open**, and this is a real mismatch. FR-032 covers 006's requirements "that mandate an approval before every phase", which fits 006 FR-010 and FR-011. But the Supersession record also supersedes **006 FR-013**, which is about what a proposal _states_ — the delta row — not about approval. No requirement accounts for that one, so FR-032 and FR-033 together do leave a superseded requirement unaddressed.

## Requirement Completeness — gaps

- [ ] CHK027 Does the specification say when and how a maintainer exercises FR-007's override — before the run starts, at any approval, or both? [Gap, Spec §FR-007] **Open**: FR-007 states the override exists and does not say when or how it is exercised — before the run, at any approval, or both. `research.md` R5 and the `gate_mode` field settle it in the implementation; the requirement does not.
- [x] CHK028 Does FR-007 state whether the override persists for the whole run or applies to a single phase? [Gap, Spec §FR-007] **Reviewed 2026-09-05**: yes. FR-007's "require an approval before every phase **for a run**" states the scope: the whole run, not a single phase.
- [ ] CHK029 Is a minimum number of alternatives specified for FR-013, or would a single "approach" satisfy an offer of "alternatives"? [Completeness, Spec §FR-013] **Open**: FR-013 says "stated alternative remediation approaches" with no minimum, so one "approach" would arguably satisfy an offer of alternatives. `skills/ccd-pipeline-fix/SKILL.md` requires at least two; the requirement does not.
- [ ] CHK030 Does FR-017 cover the case where the maintainer wants several failing jobs addressed together rather than choosing one? [Coverage, Spec §FR-017] **Open**: FR-017 requires asking which subject to take when several could be, and does not cover a maintainer who wants several failing jobs addressed together. The requirement forces a choice the maintainer may not want to make.
- [ ] CHK031 Are requirements defined for what the capability does when the failing evidence is retrieved but empty, truncated, or expired by the forge's retention? [Gap, Edge Case] **Open**: no requirement. Retrieval succeeding but returning empty, truncated, or retention-expired evidence is neither FR-011a's success nor FR-011b's failure, so it falls between them.
- [ ] CHK032 Are requirements defined for a pipeline that fails intermittently, where one run's evidence does not establish a cause? [Gap, Edge Case] **Open**: no requirement. An intermittently failing pipeline, where one run's evidence does not establish a cause, is not covered by FR-012's "propose a root cause accompanied by the specific evidence supporting it".
- [ ] CHK033 Does the specification state who decides FR-019's "would add or alter a requirement", and at what point in the flow that decision is made? [Gap, Spec §FR-019] **Open**: FR-019 says the capability must report that the work is feature work, and does not say who decides that or at what point in the flow — before the root cause is proposed, or after an approach is chosen.
- [ ] CHK034 Are requirements defined for the FR-030 case's visibility — where a document is left unshortened, is the reason recorded durably or only reported in passing? [Gap, Spec §FR-030] **Open**: FR-030 says the reason is "reported", which a run satisfies by printing it. Nothing requires it recorded durably. It was recorded in `tasks.md` in practice, by convention rather than by requirement.
- [ ] CHK035 Does the specification address the Edge Cases entry about a phase auto-proceeding and then failing, with a requirement rather than only a narrative note? [Gap, Spec §Edge Cases] **Open**: the Edge Cases entry states the obligation in narrative and no requirement carries it. Nothing in FR-001–FR-008 covers a phase that auto-proceeded and then failed.
- [ ] CHK036 Does the specification address the Edge Cases entry about shortening removing non-normative but load-bearing context, with a requirement rather than only a narrative note? [Gap, Spec §Edge Cases, §FR-028] **Open**: same shape. The Edge Cases entry names the risk — losing a non-normative but load-bearing passage — and R1 mitigates it by classifying rationale markers as normative, but no requirement states the obligation.
- [ ] CHK037 Are requirements defined for what happens when FR-011a's retrieval succeeds but the maintainer disputes that the retrieved run is the right one? [Coverage, Gap] **Open**: no requirement. FR-011a covers retrieval and FR-017 covers ambiguity between several candidates; neither covers a maintainer disputing an unambiguous retrieval.

## Dependencies & Assumptions

- [ ] CHK038 Is the assumption that the bug-remediation workflow is "fit to receive pipeline defects unchanged" validated anywhere, given FR-014 makes the whole of User Story 2 depend on it? [Assumption, Spec §Assumptions] **Open**: stated as an Assumption and validated nowhere. FR-014 makes the whole of User Story 2 depend on it, and this repository cannot exercise it — see CHK040.
- [ ] CHK039 Is the assumption that artifact compaction "is already served by tooling the repository has installed" verifiable from the specification, given FR-027a excludes artifacts on that basis? [Assumption, Spec §FR-027a] **Open**: "already served by tooling the repository has installed" names no tooling, so the basis for FR-027a's exclusion is not verifiable from the specification.
- [ ] CHK040 Is the consequence of the assumption that this repository runs no pipeline of its own stated as a requirement — that User Story 2 cannot be verified end to end here — rather than only as an assumption? [Assumption, Traceability] **Open**: stated as an Assumption, and `quickstart.md` § Known limit records the consequence — but as a limit on validation, not as a requirement. Nothing obliges the feature to state that User Story 2 is unverified here.
- [ ] CHK041 Does the specification record what happens to this feature's own requirements if the maintainer's forge access is revoked between preflight and retrieval? [Assumption, Edge Case] **Open**: no requirement. FR-011c determines availability before the run begins and FR-011b covers retrieval failing; access revoked _between_ those two points is covered by neither in terms, though FR-011b's "the attempt fails" arguably reaches it.

## Scenario Coverage

- [ ] CHK042 Are recovery requirements defined for a run interrupted between an approval and the step it approved? [Coverage, Recovery, Gap] **Open**: no requirement. FR-005 governs what an approval permits and nothing governs an interruption between an approval and the step it approved.
- [ ] CHK043 Are requirements defined for the exception flow in which the bug-remediation workflow invoked by FR-014 itself stops or fails? [Coverage, Exception Flow, Gap] **Open**: no requirement. FR-014 mandates the dispatch and FR-016 covers validation not showing the defect resolved; the bug workflow itself stopping or failing is neither.
- [ ] CHK044 Are requirements defined for a shortening pass that is interrupted partway, leaving some documents shortened and others not? [Coverage, Recovery, Gap] **Open**: no requirement, and less pressing since FR-027's withdrawal — no multi-document pass is now mandated. It would return with any future pass covering more than one file.
- [x] CHK045 Is each of the four user stories independently deliverable as claimed, given FR-026 sequences FR-025 ahead of User Story 4 and nothing else states a cross-story order? **Resolved 2026-09-05** by `/speckit-analyze` finding F5: User Story 4 is independently testable but not independently schedulable, and `spec.md` §US4 now carries that caveat explicitly. [Consistency, Spec §US1–US4]

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation
- `/speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `/speckit-specify` and `/speckit-clarify`
- CHK020 was a genuine conflict between User Story 1's first acceptance scenario and FR-003. It was raised and resolved before planning, on 2026-09-05: FR-003's reversibility test governs, and the scenario was amended to match. It is the one item this checklist's author marked, and it is marked because the conflict it names no longer exists.
- CHK004, CHK005, CHK011, CHK012 and CHK013 all circle the same weakness: the compaction requirements rest on an undefined notion of "normative" and set no threshold for "shortened". These are the requirements most likely to be unsatisfiable as written.
- Items are numbered sequentially for easy reference
